transcript.text: Good evening, everyone. Let's get started. We've got the showcase coming up at the Harborlight Theater right after the feature-film premiere, and I need to hear from our technical director and music rights coordinator with their final checks before I can sign off on the package. Who wants to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue before we go any further. I received the completed power survey from the Harborlight electrician this morning. The theater can safely support a live band only if it is configured as six musicians — not eight — and the electrical load plan permits a maximum performance length of 75 minutes, not 90. The survey came in signed after the current production draft was circulated, so these constraints aren't reflected in the draft yet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical rights issue. I've confirmed with the publisher that 'Neon Atlas' is NOT cleared for this live showcase. The publisher has approved 'Glass River' as the replacement closing song, but the license also prohibits audience recording of the performance. I'm still waiting for the countersigned license scan before I can attach it to the show file, so the package isn't fully ready for sign-off yet.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both for flagging these issues. Let me make sure I understand the full picture before we proceed. Rafael, the signed power survey from the Harborlight electrician limits us to six musicians and 75 minutes maximum — both of which conflict with our current draft. June, the publisher has not cleared 'Neon Atlas,' but has approved 'Glass River' as a replacement closing song, with the additional constraint that audience recording is now prohibited. And you're still waiting on the countersigned license scan before the show file is complete. So to summarize the changes from our current draft: band goes from eight to six, performance from 90 to 75 minutes, closing song changes from 'Neon Atlas' to 'Glass River,' and audience recording permission is revoked. Are there any other outstanding items either of you need to report, or is this the complete set of issues? Once I have the countersigned license in hand, I can sign off on the revised package.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: That's the complete set of issues from my side, Morgan. The power survey constraints — six musicians and 75 minutes — are the only outstanding technical items I have. I haven't entered them into the production draft yet since the signed survey arrived after circulation, but I'll update the draft as soon as we've agreed on the revisions here. I don't have any other outstanding items to report.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: That's the complete set of issues from my side as well, Morgan. The only outstanding item I have is the countersigned license scan for 'Glass River' — once I receive it, I'll attach it to the show file and the package will be ready for your sign-off. No other rights issues to report.
